items.title: Bucky Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: they asked me to do it with Skitch Henderson... I’m doing a couple of symphony dates with Skitch Henderson in Florida

ctx.x: Less arranged almost. © Fillius Jazz Archive -9-

Yeah. And then the set groups were playing now. They weren’t using studio guys. Record companies turned over the studios to a group. Now the group would sit around all day long trying to make a track. A rhythm track. And nobody could get in — Mitch Miller couldn’t get into his own studios down there because some group was sitting there trying to make rhythm tracks, and they’re subtracting and adding — take this out, put this in— waste of time. Big waste of time and money. So I didn’t want to get in on that so…
And what was the schedule like for that show?

items.title: Skitch Henderson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Milford, Connecticut, October 31, 1998
items.q: That, Bucky and I, Bucky Pizzarelli and I talk about. Because Bucky was good to the end.

ctx.x: And Bucky of course I knew from the Vaughan Monroe Orchestra. So it wasn’t me, I had a commitment to change the style of the orchestra and to do that, you know you have to start from scratch and I was so fortunate to have these type of players who still had enthusiasm for playing. And then one of my jobs was to do the service shows, The Today Show and The Tonight Show. I mean I did specials, but The Tonight Show, I was stuck in the pit for a long time. And then having Steve Allen, who loved this and was learning…

items.title: Bucky Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 23, 2003 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: I do some pop dates once in a while with Skitch Henderson.

ctx.x: I mean it. That was one of the most thrilling records I ever made with those guys. And then I’ve got some — I do some pop dates once in a while with Skitch Henderson. I do some with Palm Beach Pops. I’m going to do something in Syracuse this summer. © Fillius Jazz Archive -18-
Right. With the symphony, that’s right.
